5139	 * perform that step, if required, as part of the atomic update of the
5140	 * whole transaction tree at top level commit or abort.
5141	 */ view japanese
5142
5143	/* Post-commit cleanup */ view japanese
5144	if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5145		AtSubCommit_childXids();
5146	AfterTriggerEndSubXact(true);
5147	AtSubCommit_Portals(s->subTransactionId,
5148						s->parent->subTransactionId,
5149						s->parent->nestingLevel,
5150						s->parent->curTransactionOwner);
5151	AtEOSubXact_LargeObject(true, s->subTransactionId,
5152							s->parent->subTransactionId);
5153	AtSubCommit_Notify();
5154
5155	CallSubXactCallbacks(SUBXACT_EVENT_COMMIT_SUB, s->subTransactionId,
5156						 s->parent->subTransactionId);
5157
5158	ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5159						 RESOURCE_RELEASE_BEFORE_LOCKS,
5160						 true, false);
5161	AtEOSubXact_RelationCache(true, s->subTransactionId,
5162							  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5163	AtEOSubXact_TypeCache();
5164	AtEOSubXact_Inval(true);
5165	AtSubCommit_smgr();
5166
5167	/*
5168	 * The only lock we actually release here is the subtransaction XID lock.
5169	 */ view japanese
5170	CurrentResourceOwner = s->curTransactionOwner;
5171	if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5172		XactLockTableDelete(XidFromFullTransactionId(s->fullTransactionId));
5173
5174	/*
5175	 * Other locks should get transferred to their parent resource owner.
5176	 */ view japanese
5177	ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5178						 RESOURCE_RELEASE_LOCKS,
5179						 true, false);
5180	ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5181						 RESOURCE_RELEASE_AFTER_LOCKS,
5182						 true, false);
5183
5184	AtEOXact_GUC(true, s->gucNestLevel);
5185	AtEOSubXact_SPI(true, s->subTransactionId);
5186	AtEOSubXact_on_commit_actions(true, s->subTransactionId,
5187								  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5188	AtEOSubXact_Namespace(true, s->subTransactionId,
5189						  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5190	AtEOSubXact_Files(true, s->subTransactionId,
5191					  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5192	AtEOSubXact_HashTables(true, s->nestingLevel);
5193	AtEOSubXact_PgStat(true, s->nestingLevel);
5194	AtSubCommit_Snapshot(s->nestingLevel);
5195
5196	/*
5197	 * We need to restore the upper transaction's read-only state, in case the
5198	 * upper is read-write while the child is read-only; GUC will incorrectly
5199	 * think it should leave the child state in place.
5200	 */ view japanese
5201	XactReadOnly = s->prevXactReadOnly;
5202
5203	CurrentResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5204	CurTransactionResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5205	ResourceOwnerDelete(s->curTransactionOwner);
5206	s->curTransactionOwner = NULL;
5207
5208	AtSubCommit_Memory();
5209
5210	s->state = TRANS_DEFAULT;
5211
5212	PopTransaction();
5213}
5214
5215/*
5216 * AbortSubTransaction
5217 */ view japanese
5218static void
5219AbortSubTransaction(void)
5220{
5221	TransactionState s = CurrentTransactionState;
5222
5223	/* Prevent cancel/die interrupt while cleaning up */ view japanese
5224	HOLD_INTERRUPTS();
5225
5226	/* Make sure we have a valid memory context and resource owner */ view japanese
5227	AtSubAbort_Memory();
5228	AtSubAbort_ResourceOwner();
5229
5230	/*
5231	 * Release any LW locks we might be holding as quickly as possible.
5232	 * (Regular locks, however, must be held till we finish aborting.)
5233	 * Releasing LW locks is critical since we might try to grab them again
5234	 * while cleaning up!
5235	 *
5236	 * FIXME This may be incorrect --- Are there some locks we should keep?
5237	 * Buffer locks, for example?  I don't think so but I'm not sure.
5238	 */ view japanese
5239	LWLockReleaseAll();
5240
5241	pgstat_report_wait_end();
5242	pgstat_progress_end_command();
5243
5244	pgaio_error_cleanup();
5245
5246	UnlockBuffers();
5247
5248	/* Reset WAL record construction state */ view japanese
5249	XLogResetInsertion();
5250
5251	/* Cancel condition variable sleep */ view japanese
5252	ConditionVariableCancelSleep();
5253
5254	/*
5255	 * Also clean up any open wait for lock, since the lock manager will choke
5256	 * if we try to wait for another lock before doing this.
5257	 */ view japanese
5258	LockErrorCleanup();
5259
5260	/*
5261	 * If any timeout events are still active, make sure the timeout interrupt
5262	 * is scheduled.  This covers possible loss of a timeout interrupt due to
5263	 * longjmp'ing out of the SIGINT handler (see notes in handle_sig_alarm).
5264	 * We delay this till after LockErrorCleanup so that we don't uselessly
5265	 * reschedule lock or deadlock check timeouts.
5266	 */ view japanese
5267	reschedule_timeouts();
5268
5269	/*
5270	 * Re-enable signals, in case we got here by longjmp'ing out of a signal
5271	 * handler.  We do this fairly early in the sequence so that the timeout
5272	 * infrastructure will be functional if needed while aborting.
5273	 */ view japanese
5274	sigprocmask(SIG_SETMASK, &UnBlockSig, NULL);
5275
5276	/*
5277	 * check the current transaction state
5278	 */ view japanese
5279	ShowTransactionState("AbortSubTransaction");
5280
5281	if (s->state != TRANS_INPROGRESS)
5282		elog(WARNING, "AbortSubTransaction while in %s state",
5283			 TransStateAsString(s->state));
5284
5285	s->state = TRANS_ABORT;
5286
5287	/*
5288	 * Reset user ID which might have been changed transiently.  (See notes in
5289	 * AbortTransaction.)
5290	 */ view japanese
5291	SetUserIdAndSecContext(s->prevUser, s->prevSecContext);
5292
5293	/* Forget about any active REINDEX. */ view japanese
5294	ResetReindexState(s->nestingLevel);
5295
5296	/* Reset logical streaming state. */ view japanese
5297	ResetLogicalStreamingState();
5298
5299	/*
5300	 * No need for SnapBuildResetExportedSnapshotState() here, snapshot
5301	 * exports are not supported in subtransactions.
5302	 */ view japanese
5303
5304	/*
5305	 * If this subxact has started any unfinished parallel operation, clean up
5306	 * its workers and exit parallel mode.  Don't warn about leaked resources.
5307	 */ view japanese
5308	AtEOSubXact_Parallel(false, s->subTransactionId);
5309	s->parallelModeLevel = 0;
5310
5311	/*
5312	 * We can skip all this stuff if the subxact failed before creating a
5313	 * ResourceOwner...
5314	 */ view japanese
5315	if (s->curTransactionOwner)
5316	{
5317		AfterTriggerEndSubXact(false);
5318		AtSubAbort_Portals(s->subTransactionId,
5319						   s->parent->subTransactionId,
5320						   s->curTransactionOwner,
5321						   s->parent->curTransactionOwner);
5322		AtEOSubXact_LargeObject(false, s->subTransactionId,
5323								s->parent->subTransactionId);
5324		AtSubAbort_Notify();
5325
5326		/* Advertise the fact that we aborted in pg_xact. */ view japanese
5327		(void) RecordTransactionAbort(true);
5328
5329		/* Post-abort cleanup */ view japanese
5330		if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5331			AtSubAbort_childXids();
5332
5333		CallSubXactCallbacks(SUBXACT_EVENT_ABORT_SUB, s->subTransactionId,
5334							 s->parent->subTransactionId);
5335
5336		ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5337							 RESOURCE_RELEASE_BEFORE_LOCKS,
5338							 false, false);
5339
5340		AtEOXact_Aio(false);
5341		AtEOSubXact_RelationCache(false, s->subTransactionId,
5342								  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5343		AtEOSubXact_TypeCache();
5344		AtEOSubXact_Inval(false);
5345		ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5346							 RESOURCE_RELEASE_LOCKS,
5347							 false, false);
5348		ResourceOwnerRelease(s->curTransactionOwner,
5349							 RESOURCE_RELEASE_AFTER_LOCKS,
5350							 false, false);
5351		AtSubAbort_smgr();
5352
5353		AtEOXact_GUC(false, s->gucNestLevel);
5354		AtEOSubXact_SPI(false, s->subTransactionId);
5355		AtEOSubXact_on_commit_actions(false, s->subTransactionId,
5356									  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5357		AtEOSubXact_Namespace(false, s->subTransactionId,
5358							  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5359		AtEOSubXact_Files(false, s->subTransactionId,
5360						  s->parent->subTransactionId);
5361		AtEOSubXact_HashTables(false, s->nestingLevel);
5362		AtEOSubXact_PgStat(false, s->nestingLevel);
5363		AtSubAbort_Snapshot(s->nestingLevel);
5364	}
5365
5366	/*
5367	 * Restore the upper transaction's read-only state, too.  This should be
5368	 * redundant with GUC's cleanup but we may as well do it for consistency
5369	 * with the commit case.
5370	 */ view japanese
5371	XactReadOnly = s->prevXactReadOnly;
5372
5373	RESUME_INTERRUPTS();
5374}
5375
5376/*
5377 * CleanupSubTransaction
5378 *
5379 *	The caller has to make sure to always reassign CurrentTransactionState
5380 *	if it has a local pointer to it after calling this function.
5381 */ view japanese
5382static void
5383CleanupSubTransaction(void)
5384{
5385	TransactionState s = CurrentTransactionState;
5386
5387	ShowTransactionState("CleanupSubTransaction");
5388
5389	if (s->state != TRANS_ABORT)
5390		elog(WARNING, "CleanupSubTransaction while in %s state",
5391			 TransStateAsString(s->state));
5392
5393	AtSubCleanup_Portals(s->subTransactionId);
5394
5395	CurrentResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5396	CurTransactionResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5397	if (s->curTransactionOwner)
5398		ResourceOwnerDelete(s->curTransactionOwner);
5399	s->curTransactionOwner = NULL;
5400
5401	AtSubCleanup_Memory();
5402
5403	s->state = TRANS_DEFAULT;
5404
5405	PopTransaction();
5406}
5407
5408/*
5409 * PushTransaction
5410 *		Create transaction state stack entry for a subtransaction
5411 *
5412 *	The caller has to make sure to always reassign CurrentTransactionState
5413 *	if it has a local pointer to it after calling this function.
5414 */ view japanese
5415static void
5416PushTransaction(void)
5417{
5418	TransactionState p = CurrentTransactionState;
5419	TransactionState s;
5420
5421	/*
5422	 * We keep subtransaction state nodes in TopTransactionContext.
5423	 */ view japanese
5424	s = (TransactionState)
5425		MemoryContextAllocZero(TopTransactionContext,
5426							   sizeof(TransactionStateData));
5427
5428	/*
5429	 * Assign a subtransaction ID, watching out for counter wraparound.
5430	 */ view japanese
5431	currentSubTransactionId += 1;
5432	if (currentSubTransactionId == InvalidSubTransactionId)
5433	{
5434		currentSubTransactionId -= 1;
5435		pfree(s);
5436		ereport(ERROR,
5437				(errcode(ERRCODE_PROGRAM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED),
5438				 errmsg("cannot have more than 2^32-1 subtransactions in a transaction")));
5439	}
5440
5441	/*
5442	 * We can now stack a minimally valid subtransaction without fear of
5443	 * failure.
5444	 */ view japanese
5445	s->fullTransactionId = InvalidFullTransactionId;	/* until assigned */ view japanese
5446	s->subTransactionId = currentSubTransactionId;
5447	s->parent = p;
5448	s->nestingLevel = p->nestingLevel + 1;
5449	s->gucNestLevel = NewGUCNestLevel();
5450	s->savepointLevel = p->savepointLevel;
5451	s->state = TRANS_DEFAULT;
5452	s->blockState = TBLOCK_SUBBEGIN;
5453	GetUserIdAndSecContext(&s->prevUser, &s->prevSecContext);
5454	s->prevXactReadOnly = XactReadOnly;
5455	s->startedInRecovery = p->startedInRecovery;
5456	s->parallelModeLevel = 0;
5457	s->parallelChildXact = (p->parallelModeLevel != 0 || p->parallelChildXact);
5458	s->topXidLogged = false;
5459
5460	CurrentTransactionState = s;
5461
5462	/*
5463	 * AbortSubTransaction and CleanupSubTransaction have to be able to cope
5464	 * with the subtransaction from here on out; in particular they should not
5465	 * assume that it necessarily has a transaction context, resource owner,
5466	 * or XID.
5467	 */ view japanese
5468}
5469
5470/*
5471 * PopTransaction
5472 *		Pop back to parent transaction state
5473 *
5474 *	The caller has to make sure to always reassign CurrentTransactionState
5475 *	if it has a local pointer to it after calling this function.
5476 */ view japanese
5477static void
5478PopTransaction(void)
5479{
5480	TransactionState s = CurrentTransactionState;
5481
5482	if (s->state != TRANS_DEFAULT)
5483		elog(WARNING, "PopTransaction while in %s state",
5484			 TransStateAsString(s->state));
5485
5486	if (s->parent == NULL)
5487		elog(FATAL, "PopTransaction with no parent");
5488
5489	CurrentTransactionState = s->parent;
5490
5491	/* Let's just make sure CurTransactionContext is good */ view japanese
5492	CurTransactionContext = s->parent->curTransactionContext;
5493	MemoryContextSwitchTo(CurTransactionContext);
5494
5495	/* Ditto for ResourceOwner links */ view japanese
5496	CurTransactionResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5497	CurrentResourceOwner = s->parent->curTransactionOwner;
5498
5499	/* Free the old child structure */ view japanese
5500	if (s->name)
5501		pfree(s->name);
5502	pfree(s);
5503}
5504
5505/*
5506 * EstimateTransactionStateSpace
5507 *		Estimate the amount of space that will be needed by
5508 *		SerializeTransactionState.  It would be OK to overestimate slightly,
5509 *		but it's simple for us to work out the precise value, so we do.
5510 */ view japanese
5511Size
5512EstimateTransactionStateSpace(void)
5513{
5514	TransactionState s;
5515	Size		nxids = 0;
5516	Size		size = SerializedTransactionStateHeaderSize;
5517
5518	for (s = CurrentTransactionState; s != NULL; s = s->parent)
5519	{
5520		if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5521			nxids = add_size(nxids, 1);
5522		nxids = add_size(nxids, s->nChildXids);
5523	}
5524
5525	return add_size(size, mul_size(sizeof(TransactionId), nxids));
5526}
5527
5528/*
5529 * SerializeTransactionState
5530 *		Write out relevant details of our transaction state that will be
5531 *		needed by a parallel worker.
5532 *
5533 * We need to save and restore XactDeferrable, XactIsoLevel, and the XIDs
5534 * associated with this transaction.  These are serialized into a
5535 * caller-supplied buffer big enough to hold the number of bytes reported by
5536 * EstimateTransactionStateSpace().  We emit the XIDs in sorted order for the
5537 * convenience of the receiving process.
5538 */ view japanese
5539void
5540SerializeTransactionState(Size maxsize, char *start_address)
5541{
5542	TransactionState s;
5543	Size		nxids = 0;
5544	Size		i = 0;
5545	TransactionId *workspace;
5546	SerializedTransactionState *result;
5547
5548	result = (SerializedTransactionState *) start_address;
5549
5550	result->xactIsoLevel = XactIsoLevel;
5551	result->xactDeferrable = XactDeferrable;
5552	result->topFullTransactionId = XactTopFullTransactionId;
5553	result->currentFullTransactionId =
5554		CurrentTransactionState->fullTransactionId;
5555	result->currentCommandId = currentCommandId;
5556
5557	/*
5558	 * If we're running in a parallel worker and launching a parallel worker
5559	 * of our own, we can just pass along the information that was passed to
5560	 * us.
5561	 */ view japanese
5562	if (nParallelCurrentXids > 0)
5563	{
5564		result->nParallelCurrentXids = nParallelCurrentXids;
5565		memcpy(&result->parallelCurrentXids[0], ParallelCurrentXids,
5566			   nParallelCurrentXids * sizeof(TransactionId));
5567		return;
5568	}
5569
5570	/*
5571	 * OK, we need to generate a sorted list of XIDs that our workers should
5572	 * view as current.  First, figure out how many there are.
5573	 */ view japanese
5574	for (s = CurrentTransactionState; s != NULL; s = s->parent)
5575	{
5576		if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5577			nxids = add_size(nxids, 1);
5578		nxids = add_size(nxids, s->nChildXids);
5579	}
5580	Assert(SerializedTransactionStateHeaderSize + nxids * sizeof(TransactionId)
5581		   <= maxsize);
5582
5583	/* Copy them to our scratch space. */ view japanese
5584	workspace = palloc(nxids * sizeof(TransactionId));
5585	for (s = CurrentTransactionState; s != NULL; s = s->parent)
5586	{
5587		if (FullTransactionIdIsValid(s->fullTransactionId))
5588			workspace[i++] = XidFromFullTransactionId(s->fullTransactionId);
5589		if (s->nChildXids > 0)
5590			memcpy(&workspace[i], s->childXids,
5591				   s->nChildXids * sizeof(TransactionId));
5592		i += s->nChildXids;
5593	}
5594	Assert(i == nxids);
5595
5596	/* Sort them. */ view japanese
5597	qsort(workspace, nxids, sizeof(TransactionId), xidComparator);
5598
5599	/* Copy data into output area. */ view japanese
5600	result->nParallelCurrentXids = nxids;
5601	memcpy(&result->parallelCurrentXids[0], workspace,
5602		   nxids * sizeof(TransactionId));
5603}
5604
5605/*
5606 * StartParallelWorkerTransaction
5607 *		Start a parallel worker transaction, restoring the relevant
5608 *		transaction state serialized by SerializeTransactionState.
5609 */ view japanese
5610void
5611StartParallelWorkerTransaction(char *tstatespace)
5612{
5613	SerializedTransactionState *tstate;
5614
5615	Assert(CurrentTransactionState->blockState == TBLOCK_DEFAULT);
5616	StartTransaction();
5617
5618	tstate = (SerializedTransactionState *) tstatespace;
5619	XactIsoLevel = tstate->xactIsoLevel;
5620	XactDeferrable = tstate->xactDeferrable;
5621	XactTopFullTransactionId = tstate->topFullTransactionId;
5622	CurrentTransactionState->fullTransactionId =
5623		tstate->currentFullTransactionId;
5624	currentCommandId = tstate->currentCommandId;
5625	nParallelCurrentXids = tstate->nParallelCurrentXids;
5626	ParallelCurrentXids = &tstate->parallelCurrentXids[0];
5627
5628	CurrentTransactionState->blockState = TBLOCK_PARALLEL_INPROGRESS;
5629}
5630
5631/*
5632 * EndParallelWorkerTransaction
5633 *		End a parallel worker transaction.
5634 */ view japanese
5635void
5636EndParallelWorkerTransaction(void)
5637{
5638	Assert(CurrentTransactionState->blockState == TBLOCK_PARALLEL_INPROGRESS);
5639	CommitTransaction();
5640	CurrentTransactionState->blockState = TBLOCK_DEFAULT;
5641}

5644 * ShowTransactionState
5645 *		Debug support
5646 */ view japanese
5647static void
5648ShowTransactionState(const char *str)
5649{
5650	/* skip work if message will definitely not be printed */ view japanese
5651	if (message_level_is_interesting(DEBUG5))
5652		ShowTransactionStateRec(str, CurrentTransactionState);

5654
5655/*
5656 * ShowTransactionStateRec
5657 *		Recursive subroutine for ShowTransactionState
5658 */ view japanese
5659static void
5660ShowTransactionStateRec(const char *str, TransactionState s)
5661{
5662	StringInfoData buf;
5663
5664	if (s->parent)
5665	{
5666		/*
5667		 * Since this function recurses, it could be driven to stack overflow.
5668		 * This is just a debugging aid, so we can leave out some details
5669		 * instead of erroring out with check_stack_depth().
5670		 */ view japanese
5671		if (stack_is_too_deep())
5672			ereport(DEBUG5,
5673					(errmsg_internal("%s(%d): parent omitted to avoid stack overflow",
5674									 str, s->nestingLevel)));
5675		else
5676			ShowTransactionStateRec(str, s->parent);
5677	}
5678
5679	initStringInfo(&buf);
5680	if (s->nChildXids > 0)
5681	{
5682		int			i;
5683
5684		appendStringInfo(&buf, ", children: %u", s->childXids[0]);
5685		for (i = 1; i < s->nChildXids; i++)
5686			appendStringInfo(&buf, " %u", s->childXids[i]);
5687	}
5688	ereport(DEBUG5,
5689			(errmsg_internal("%s(%d) name: %s; blockState: %s; state: %s, xid/subid/cid: %u/%u/%u%s%s",
5690							 str, s->nestingLevel,
5691							 PointerIsValid(s->name) ? s->name : "unnamed",
5692							 BlockStateAsString(s->blockState),
5693							 TransStateAsString(s->state),
5694							 (unsigned int) XidFromFullTransactionId(s->fullTransactionId),
5695							 (unsigned int) s->subTransactionId,
5696							 (unsigned int) currentCommandId,
5697							 currentCommandIdUsed ? " (used)" : "",
5698							 buf.data)));
5699	pfree(buf.data);
5700}

5780/*
5781 * xactGetCommittedChildren
5782 *
5783 * Gets the list of committed children of the current transaction.  The return
5784 * value is the number of child transactions.  *ptr is set to point to an
5785 * array of TransactionIds.  The array is allocated in TopTransactionContext;
5786 * the caller should *not* pfree() it (this is a change from pre-8.4 code!).
5787 * If there are no subxacts, *ptr is set to NULL.
5788 */ view japanese
5789int
5790xactGetCommittedChildren(TransactionId **ptr)
5791{
5792	TransactionState s = CurrentTransactionState;
5793
5794	if (s->nChildXids == 0)
5795		*ptr = NULL;
5796	else
5797		*ptr = s->childXids;
5798
5799	return s->nChildXids;
5800}
5801
5802/*
5803 *	XLOG support routines
5804 */ view japanese
5805
5806
5807/*
5808 * Log the commit record for a plain or twophase transaction commit.
5809 *
5810 * A 2pc commit will be emitted when twophase_xid is valid, a plain one
5811 * otherwise.
5812 */ view japanese
5813XLogRecPtr
5814XactLogCommitRecord(TimestampTz commit_time,
5815					int nsubxacts, TransactionId *subxacts,
5816					int nrels, RelFileLocator *rels,
5817					int ndroppedstats, xl_xact_stats_item *droppedstats,
5818					int nmsgs, SharedInvalidationMessage *msgs,
5819					bool relcacheInval,
5820					int xactflags, TransactionId twophase_xid,
5821					const char *twophase_gid)
5822{
5823	xl_xact_commit xlrec;
5824	xl_xact_xinfo xl_xinfo;
5825	xl_xact_dbinfo xl_dbinfo;
5826	xl_xact_subxacts xl_subxacts;
5827	xl_xact_relfilelocators xl_relfilelocators;
5828	xl_xact_stats_items xl_dropped_stats;
5829	xl_xact_invals xl_invals;
5830	xl_xact_twophase xl_twophase;
5831	xl_xact_origin xl_origin;
5832	uint8		info;
5833
5834	Assert(CritSectionCount > 0);
5835
5836	xl_xinfo.xinfo = 0;
5837
5838	/* decide between a plain and 2pc commit */ view japanese
5839	if (!TransactionIdIsValid(twophase_xid))
5840		info = XLOG_XACT_COMMIT;
5841	else
5842		info = XLOG_XACT_COMMIT_PREPARED;
5843
5844	/* First figure out and collect all the information needed */
5845
5846	xlrec.xact_time = commit_time;
5847
5848	if (relcacheInval)
5849		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_COMPLETION_UPDATE_RELCACHE_FILE;
5850	if (forceSyncCommit)
5851		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_COMPLETION_FORCE_SYNC_COMMIT;
5852	if ((xactflags & XACT_FLAGS_ACQUIREDACCESSEXCLUSIVELOCK))
5853		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_AE_LOCKS;
5854
5855	/*
5856	 * Check if the caller would like to ask standbys for immediate feedback
5857	 * once this commit is applied.
5858	 */ view japanese
5859	if (synchronous_commit >= SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT_REMOTE_APPLY)
5860		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_COMPLETION_APPLY_FEEDBACK;
5861
5862	/*
5863	 * Relcache invalidations requires information about the current database
5864	 * and so does logical decoding.
5865	 */ view japanese
5866	if (nmsgs > 0 || XLogLogicalInfoActive())
5867	{
5868		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_DBINFO;
5869		xl_dbinfo.dbId = MyDatabaseId;
5870		xl_dbinfo.tsId = MyDatabaseTableSpace;
5871	}
5872
5873	if (nsubxacts > 0)
5874	{
5875		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_SUBXACTS;
5876		xl_subxacts.nsubxacts = nsubxacts;
5877	}
5878
5879	if (nrels > 0)
5880	{
5881		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_RELFILELOCATORS;
5882		xl_relfilelocators.nrels = nrels;
5883		info |= XLR_SPECIAL_REL_UPDATE;
5884	}
5885
5886	if (ndroppedstats > 0)
5887	{
5888		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_DROPPED_STATS;
5889		xl_dropped_stats.nitems = ndroppedstats;
5890	}
5891
5892	if (nmsgs > 0)
5893	{
5894		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_INVALS;
5895		xl_invals.nmsgs = nmsgs;
5896	}
5897
5898	if (TransactionIdIsValid(twophase_xid))
5899	{
5900		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_TWOPHASE;
5901		xl_twophase.xid = twophase_xid;
5902		Assert(twophase_gid != NULL);
5903
5904		if (XLogLogicalInfoActive())
5905			xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_GID;
5906	}
5907
5908	/* dump transaction origin information */ view japanese
5909	if (replorigin_session_origin != InvalidRepOriginId)
5910	{
5911		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN;
5912
5913		xl_origin.origin_lsn = replorigin_session_origin_lsn;
5914		xl_origin.origin_timestamp = replorigin_session_origin_timestamp;
5915	}
5916
5917	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo != 0)
5918		info |= XLOG_XACT_HAS_INFO;
5919
5920	/* Then include all the collected data into the commit record. */ view japanese
5921
5922	XLogBeginInsert();
5923
5924	XLogRegisterData(&xlrec, sizeof(xl_xact_commit));
5925
5926	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo != 0)
5927		XLogRegisterData(&xl_xinfo.xinfo, sizeof(xl_xinfo.xinfo));
5928
5929	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_DBINFO)
5930		XLogRegisterData(&xl_dbinfo, sizeof(xl_dbinfo));
5931
5932	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_SUBXACTS)
5933	{
5934		XLogRegisterData(&xl_subxacts,
5935						 MinSizeOfXactSubxacts);
5936		XLogRegisterData(subxacts,
5937						 nsubxacts * sizeof(TransactionId));
5938	}
5939
5940	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_RELFILELOCATORS)
5941	{
5942		XLogRegisterData(&xl_relfilelocators,
5943						 MinSizeOfXactRelfileLocators);
5944		XLogRegisterData(rels,
5945						 nrels * sizeof(RelFileLocator));
5946	}
5947
5948	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_DROPPED_STATS)
5949	{
5950		XLogRegisterData(&xl_dropped_stats,
5951						 MinSizeOfXactStatsItems);
5952		XLogRegisterData(droppedstats,
5953						 ndroppedstats * sizeof(xl_xact_stats_item));
5954	}
5955
5956	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_INVALS)
5957	{
5958		XLogRegisterData(&xl_invals, MinSizeOfXactInvals);
5959		XLogRegisterData(msgs,

5979/*
5980 * Log the commit record for a plain or twophase transaction abort.
5981 *
5982 * A 2pc abort will be emitted when twophase_xid is valid, a plain one
5983 * otherwise.
5984 */ view japanese
5985XLogRecPtr
5986XactLogAbortRecord(TimestampTz abort_time,
5987				   int nsubxacts, TransactionId *subxacts,
5988				   int nrels, RelFileLocator *rels,
5989				   int ndroppedstats, xl_xact_stats_item *droppedstats,
5990				   int xactflags, TransactionId twophase_xid,
5991				   const char *twophase_gid)
5992{
5993	xl_xact_abort xlrec;

5995	xl_xact_subxacts xl_subxacts;
5996	xl_xact_relfilelocators xl_relfilelocators;
5997	xl_xact_stats_items xl_dropped_stats;
5998	xl_xact_twophase xl_twophase;
5999	xl_xact_dbinfo xl_dbinfo;
6000	xl_xact_origin xl_origin;
6001
6002	uint8		info;
6003
6004	Assert(CritSectionCount > 0);
6005
6006	xl_xinfo.xinfo = 0;
6007
6008	/* decide between a plain and 2pc abort */ view japanese
6009	if (!TransactionIdIsValid(twophase_xid))
6010		info = XLOG_XACT_ABORT;
6011	else
6012		info = XLOG_XACT_ABORT_PREPARED;
6013
6014
6015	/* First figure out and collect all the information needed */ view japanese
6016
6017	xlrec.xact_time = abort_time;
6018
6019	if ((xactflags & XACT_FLAGS_ACQUIREDACCESSEXCLUSIVELOCK))
6020		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_AE_LOCKS;
6021
6022	if (nsubxacts > 0)
6023	{
6024		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_SUBXACTS;
6025		xl_subxacts.nsubxacts = nsubxacts;
6026	}
6027
6028	if (nrels > 0)
6029	{
6030		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_RELFILELOCATORS;
6031		xl_relfilelocators.nrels = nrels;
6032		info |= XLR_SPECIAL_REL_UPDATE;
6033	}
6034
6035	if (ndroppedstats > 0)
6036	{

6039	}

6041	if (TransactionIdIsValid(twophase_xid))
6042	{

6049	}

6051	if (TransactionIdIsValid(twophase_xid) && XLogLogicalInfoActive())
6052	{
6053		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_DBINFO;
6054		xl_dbinfo.dbId = MyDatabaseId;
6055		xl_dbinfo.tsId = MyDatabaseTableSpace;
6056	}
6057
6058	/*
6059	 * Dump transaction origin information. We need this during recovery to
6060	 * update the replication origin progress.
6061	 */ view japanese
6062	if (replorigin_session_origin != InvalidRepOriginId)
6063	{
6064		xl_xinfo.xinfo |= XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN;
6065
6066		xl_origin.origin_lsn = replorigin_session_origin_lsn;
6067		xl_origin.origin_timestamp = replorigin_session_origin_timestamp;
6068	}
6069
6070	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo != 0)
6071		info |= XLOG_XACT_HAS_INFO;

6074
6075	XLogBeginInsert();
6076
6077	XLogRegisterData(&xlrec, MinSizeOfXactAbort);
6078
6079	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo != 0)
6080		XLogRegisterData(&xl_xinfo, sizeof(xl_xinfo));
6081
6082	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_DBINFO)
6083		XLogRegisterData(&xl_dbinfo, sizeof(xl_dbinfo));
6084
6085	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_SUBXACTS)
6086	{
6087		XLogRegisterData(&xl_subxacts,
6088						 MinSizeOfXactSubxacts);

6090						 nsubxacts * sizeof(TransactionId));
6091	}
6092
6093	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_RELFILELOCATORS)
6094	{
6095		XLogRegisterData(&xl_relfilelocators,
6096						 MinSizeOfXactRelfileLocators);
6097		XLogRegisterData(rels,
6098						 nrels * sizeof(RelFileLocator));
6099	}

6101	if (xl_xinfo.xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_DROPPED_STATS)

6125/*
6126 * Before 9.0 this was a fairly short function, but now it performs many
6127 * actions for which the order of execution is critical.
6128 */ view japanese
6129static void
6130xact_redo_commit(xl_xact_parsed_commit *parsed,
6131				 TransactionId xid,
6132				 XLogRecPtr lsn,
6133				 RepOriginId origin_id)
6134{
6135	TransactionId max_xid;
6136	TimestampTz commit_time;
6137
6138	Assert(TransactionIdIsValid(xid));
6139
6140	max_xid = TransactionIdLatest(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6141
6142	/* Make sure nextXid is beyond any XID mentioned in the record. */
6143	AdvanceNextFullTransactionIdPastXid(max_xid);
6144
6145	Assert(((parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN) == 0) ==
6146		   (origin_id == InvalidRepOriginId));
6147
6148	if (parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN)
6149		commit_time = parsed->origin_timestamp;
6150	else
6151		commit_time = parsed->xact_time;
6152
6153	/* Set the transaction commit timestamp and metadata */ view japanese
6154	TransactionTreeSetCommitTsData(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts,
6155								   commit_time, origin_id);
6156
6157	if (standbyState == STANDBY_DISABLED)
6158	{
6159		/*
6160		 * Mark the transaction committed in pg_xact.
6161		 */ view japanese
6162		TransactionIdCommitTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6163	}
6164	else
6165	{
6166		/*
6167		 * If a transaction completion record arrives that has as-yet
6168		 * unobserved subtransactions then this will not have been fully
6169		 * handled by the call to RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds() in the
6170		 * main recovery loop in xlog.c. So we need to do bookkeeping again to
6171		 * cover that case. This is confusing and it is easy to think this
6172		 * call is irrelevant, which has happened three times in development
6173		 * already. Leave it in.
6174		 */
6175		RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds(max_xid);
6176
6177		/*
6178		 * Mark the transaction committed in pg_xact. We use async commit
6179		 * protocol during recovery to provide information on database
6180		 * consistency for when users try to set hint bits. It is important
6181		 * that we do not set hint bits until the minRecoveryPoint is past
6182		 * this commit record. This ensures that if we crash we don't see hint
6183		 * bits set on changes made by transactions that haven't yet
6184		 * recovered. It's unlikely but it's good to be safe.
6185		 */ view japanese
6186		TransactionIdAsyncCommitTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts, lsn);
6187
6188		/*
6189		 * We must mark clog before we update the ProcArray.
6190		 */ view japanese
6191		ExpireTreeKnownAssignedTransactionIds(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts, max_xid);
6192
6193		/*
6194		 * Send any cache invalidations attached to the commit. We must
6195		 * maintain the same order of invalidation then release locks as
6196		 * occurs in CommitTransaction().
6197		 */ view japanese
6198		ProcessCommittedInvalidationMessages(parsed->msgs, parsed->nmsgs,
6199											 XactCompletionRelcacheInitFileInval(parsed->xinfo),
6200											 parsed->dbId, parsed->tsId);
6201
6202		/*
6203		 * Release locks, if any. We do this for both two phase and normal one
6204		 * phase transactions. In effect we are ignoring the prepare phase and
6205		 * just going straight to lock release.
6206		 */ view japanese
6207		if (parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_AE_LOCKS)
6208			StandbyReleaseLockTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6209	}
6210
6211	if (parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN)
6212	{
6213		/* recover apply progress */
6214		replorigin_advance(origin_id, parsed->origin_lsn, lsn,
6215						   false /* backward */ , false /* WAL */ );
6216	}
6217
6218	/* Make sure files supposed to be dropped are dropped */
6219	if (parsed->nrels > 0)
6220	{
6221		/*
6222		 * First update minimum recovery point to cover this WAL record. Once
6223		 * a relation is deleted, there's no going back. The buffer manager
6224		 * enforces the WAL-first rule for normal updates to relation files,
6225		 * so that the minimum recovery point is always updated before the
6226		 * corresponding change in the data file is flushed to disk, but we
6227		 * have to do the same here since we're bypassing the buffer manager.
6228		 *
6229		 * Doing this before deleting the files means that if a deletion fails
6230		 * for some reason, you cannot start up the system even after restart,
6231		 * until you fix the underlying situation so that the deletion will
6232		 * succeed. Alternatively, we could update the minimum recovery point
6233		 * after deletion, but that would leave a small window where the
6234		 * WAL-first rule would be violated.
6235		 */ view japanese
6236		XLogFlush(lsn);
6237
6238		/* Make sure files supposed to be dropped are dropped */
6239		DropRelationFiles(parsed->xlocators, parsed->nrels, true);
6240	}
6241
6242	if (parsed->nstats > 0)
6243	{
6244		/* see equivalent call for relations above */
6245		XLogFlush(lsn);
6246
6247		pgstat_execute_transactional_drops(parsed->nstats, parsed->stats, true);
6248	}
6249
6250	/*
6251	 * We issue an XLogFlush() for the same reason we emit ForceSyncCommit()
6252	 * in normal operation. For example, in CREATE DATABASE, we copy all files
6253	 * from the template database, and then commit the transaction. If we
6254	 * crash after all the files have been copied but before the commit, you
6255	 * have files in the data directory without an entry in pg_database. To
6256	 * minimize the window for that, we use ForceSyncCommit() to rush the
6257	 * commit record to disk as quick as possible. We have the same window
6258	 * during recovery, and forcing an XLogFlush() (which updates
6259	 * minRecoveryPoint during recovery) helps to reduce that problem window,
6260	 * for any user that requested ForceSyncCommit().
6261	 */ view japanese
6262	if (XactCompletionForceSyncCommit(parsed->xinfo))
6263		XLogFlush(lsn);
6264
6265	/*
6266	 * If asked by the primary (because someone is waiting for a synchronous
6267	 * commit = remote_apply), we will need to ask walreceiver to send a reply
6268	 * immediately.
6269	 */ view japanese
6270	if (XactCompletionApplyFeedback(parsed->xinfo))
6271		XLogRequestWalReceiverReply();
6272}
6273
6274/*
6275 * Be careful with the order of execution, as with xact_redo_commit().
6276 * The two functions are similar but differ in key places.
6277 *
6278 * Note also that an abort can be for a subtransaction and its children,
6279 * not just for a top level abort. That means we have to consider
6280 * topxid != xid, whereas in commit we would find topxid == xid always
6281 * because subtransaction commit is never WAL logged.
6282 */ view japanese
6283static void
6284xact_redo_abort(xl_xact_parsed_abort *parsed, TransactionId xid,
6285				XLogRecPtr lsn, RepOriginId origin_id)
6286{
6287	TransactionId max_xid;
6288
6289	Assert(TransactionIdIsValid(xid));
6290
6291	/* Make sure nextXid is beyond any XID mentioned in the record. */ view japanese
6292	max_xid = TransactionIdLatest(xid,
6293								  parsed->nsubxacts,
6294								  parsed->subxacts);
6295	AdvanceNextFullTransactionIdPastXid(max_xid);
6296
6297	if (standbyState == STANDBY_DISABLED)
6298	{
6299		/* Mark the transaction aborted in pg_xact, no need for async stuff */
6300		TransactionIdAbortTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6301	}
6302	else
6303	{
6304		/*
6305		 * If a transaction completion record arrives that has as-yet
6306		 * unobserved subtransactions then this will not have been fully
6307		 * handled by the call to RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds() in the
6308		 * main recovery loop in xlog.c. So we need to do bookkeeping again to
6309		 * cover that case. This is confusing and it is easy to think this
6310		 * call is irrelevant, which has happened three times in development
6311		 * already. Leave it in.
6312		 */ view japanese
6313		RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds(max_xid);
6314
6315		/* Mark the transaction aborted in pg_xact, no need for async stuff */ view japanese
6316		TransactionIdAbortTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6317
6318		/*
6319		 * We must update the ProcArray after we have marked clog.
6320		 */ view japanese
6321		ExpireTreeKnownAssignedTransactionIds(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts, max_xid);
6322
6323		/*
6324		 * There are no invalidation messages to send or undo.
6325		 */ view japanese
6326
6327		/*
6328		 * Release locks, if any. There are no invalidations to send.
6329		 */ view japanese
6330		if (parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_AE_LOCKS)
6331			StandbyReleaseLockTree(xid, parsed->nsubxacts, parsed->subxacts);
6332	}
6333
6334	if (parsed->xinfo & XACT_XINFO_HAS_ORIGIN)
6335	{
6336		/* recover apply progress */ view japanese
6337		replorigin_advance(origin_id, parsed->origin_lsn, lsn,
6338						   false /* backward */ , false /* WAL */ ); view japanese view japanese
6339	}
6340
6341	/* Make sure files supposed to be dropped are dropped */ view japanese
6342	if (parsed->nrels > 0)
6343	{
6344		/*
6345		 * See comments about update of minimum recovery point on truncation,
6346		 * in xact_redo_commit().
6347		 */ view japanese
6348		XLogFlush(lsn);
6349
6350		DropRelationFiles(parsed->xlocators, parsed->nrels, true);
6351	}
6352
6353	if (parsed->nstats > 0)
6354	{
6355		/* see equivalent call for relations above */ view japanese
6356		XLogFlush(lsn);
6357
6358		pgstat_execute_transactional_drops(parsed->nstats, parsed->stats, true);
6359	}
6360}

6362void
6363xact_redo(XLogReaderState *record)
6364{
6365	uint8		info = XLogRecGetInfo(record) & XLOG_XACT_OPMASK;
6366
6367	/* Backup blocks are not used in xact records */ view japanese
6368	Assert(!XLogRecHasAnyBlockRefs(record));
6369
6370	if (info == XLOG_XACT_COMMIT)
6371	{
6372		xl_xact_commit *xlrec = (xl_xact_commit *) XLogRecGetData(record);
6373		xl_xact_parsed_commit parsed;
6374
6375		ParseCommitRecord(XLogRecGetInfo(record), xlrec, &parsed);
6376		xact_redo_commit(&parsed, XLogRecGetXid(record),
6377						 record->EndRecPtr, XLogRecGetOrigin(record));
6378	}
6379	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_COMMIT_PREPARED)
6380	{
6381		xl_xact_commit *xlrec = (xl_xact_commit *) XLogRecGetData(record);
6382		xl_xact_parsed_commit parsed;
6383
6384		ParseCommitRecord(XLogRecGetInfo(record), xlrec, &parsed);
6385		xact_redo_commit(&parsed, parsed.twophase_xid,
6386						 record->EndRecPtr, XLogRecGetOrigin(record));
6387
6388		/* Delete TwoPhaseState gxact entry and/or 2PC file. */
6389		LWLockAcquire(TwoPhaseStateLock, LW_EXCLUSIVE);
6390		PrepareRedoRemove(parsed.twophase_xid, false);
6391		LWLockRelease(TwoPhaseStateLock);
6392	}
6393	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_ABORT)
6394	{
6395		xl_xact_abort *xlrec = (xl_xact_abort *) XLogRecGetData(record);
6396		xl_xact_parsed_abort parsed;
6397
6398		ParseAbortRecord(XLogRecGetInfo(record), xlrec, &parsed);
6399		xact_redo_abort(&parsed, XLogRecGetXid(record),
6400						record->EndRecPtr, XLogRecGetOrigin(record));
6401	}
6402	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_ABORT_PREPARED)
6403	{
6404		xl_xact_abort *xlrec = (xl_xact_abort *) XLogRecGetData(record);
6405		xl_xact_parsed_abort parsed;
6406
6407		ParseAbortRecord(XLogRecGetInfo(record), xlrec, &parsed);
6408		xact_redo_abort(&parsed, parsed.twophase_xid,
6409						record->EndRecPtr, XLogRecGetOrigin(record));
6410
6411		/* Delete TwoPhaseState gxact entry and/or 2PC file. */ view japanese
6412		LWLockAcquire(TwoPhaseStateLock, LW_EXCLUSIVE);
6413		PrepareRedoRemove(parsed.twophase_xid, false);
6414		LWLockRelease(TwoPhaseStateLock);
6415	}
6416	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_PREPARE)
6417	{
6418		/*
6419		 * Store xid and start/end pointers of the WAL record in TwoPhaseState
6420		 * gxact entry.
6421		 */ view japanese
6422		LWLockAcquire(TwoPhaseStateLock, LW_EXCLUSIVE);
6423		PrepareRedoAdd(XLogRecGetData(record),
6424					   record->ReadRecPtr,
6425					   record->EndRecPtr,
6426					   XLogRecGetOrigin(record));
6427		LWLockRelease(TwoPhaseStateLock);
6428	}
6429	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_ASSIGNMENT)
6430	{
6431		xl_xact_assignment *xlrec = (xl_xact_assignment *) XLogRecGetData(record);
6432
6433		if (standbyState >= STANDBY_INITIALIZED)
6434			ProcArrayApplyXidAssignment(xlrec->xtop,
6435										xlrec->nsubxacts, xlrec->xsub);
6436	}
6437	else if (info == XLOG_XACT_INVALIDATIONS)
6438	{
6439		/*
6440		 * XXX we do ignore this for now, what matters are invalidations
6441		 * written into the commit record.
6442		 */ view japanese
6443	}
6444	else
6445		elog(PANIC, "xact_redo: unknown op code %u", info);
6446}

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:89-98

/*
 * CheckXidAlive は、進行中の可能性がある（サブ）トランザクションを指す xid 値です。現在、これは論理デコードで使用されています。デコードの進行中にそのようなトランザクションがアボートされる可能性があるため、その場合は特定のトランザクションのデコードをスキップします。これを確実にするため、システムテーブルからタプルを取得した後に CheckXidAlive がアボートされているかどうかを確認します。また、論理デコード中に tableam や heap API に直接アクセスしないようにしています。これは、systable_* API においてのみ同時アボートのチェックを行っているためです。
 */

Original comment

/*
 * CheckXidAlive is a xid value pointing to a possibly ongoing (sub)
 * transaction.  Currently, it is used in logical decoding.  It's possible
 * that such transactions can get aborted while the decoding is ongoing in
 * which case we skip decoding that particular transaction.  To ensure that we
 * check whether the CheckXidAlive is aborted after fetching the tuple from
 * system tables.  We also ensure that during logical decoding we never
 * directly access the tableam or heap APIs because we are checking for the
 * concurrent aborts only in systable_* APIs.
 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:102-124

/*
 * パラレルワーカーとして実行される場合、パラレルワーカーの状態スタックには単一の
 * TransactionStateData のみを配置します。そこに反映される XID は、並列処理を開始した
 * バックエンドにおける、現在アクティブな *最も内側の* サブトランザクションのものとなります。
 * しかし、GetTopTransactionId() および TransactionIdIsCurrentTransactionId() は、
 * ユーザーバックエンドで行う場合と同じ結果をパラレルワーカーでも返す必要があるため、
 * 追加のブックキーピングが必要となります。
 *
 * XactTopFullTransactionId はトップレベルトランザクションの XID を格納します。これは通常の
 * バックエンドでは TopTransactionStateData.fullTransactionId と同じになりますが、
 * トランザクション状態全体を持たないパラレルバックエンドでは、並列操作を開始したバックエンドから
 * コピーされたものとなります。
 *
 * 通常のバックエンドでは nParallelCurrentXids は 0、ParallelCurrentXids は NULL となりますが、
 * パラレルバックエンドでは、nParallelCurrentXids に現在とみなされるべき XID の数が格納され、
 * ParallelCurrentXids にそれらの XID 自体が格納されます。これには、並列操作が開始された時点で
 * 親において現在アクティブであった、またはサブコミットされていたすべての XID が含まれます。
 * XID は、ルックアップを可能な限り高速化するために、（論理順序ではなく）数値順にソートされて
 * 格納されます。

/*
 * When running as a parallel worker, we place only a single
 * TransactionStateData on the parallel worker's state stack, and the XID
 * reflected there will be that of the *innermost* currently-active
 * subtransaction in the backend that initiated parallelism.  However,
 * GetTopTransactionId() and TransactionIdIsCurrentTransactionId()
 * need to return the same answers in the parallel worker as they would have
 * in the user backend, so we need some additional bookkeeping.
 *
 * XactTopFullTransactionId stores the XID of our toplevel transaction, which
 * will be the same as TopTransactionStateData.fullTransactionId in an
 * ordinary backend; but in a parallel backend, which does not have the entire
 * transaction state, it will instead be copied from the backend that started
 * the parallel operation.
 *
 * nParallelCurrentXids will be 0 and ParallelCurrentXids NULL in an ordinary
 * backend, but in a parallel backend, nParallelCurrentXids will contain the
 * number of XIDs that need to be considered current, and ParallelCurrentXids
 * will contain the XIDs themselves.  This includes all XIDs that were current
 * or sub-committed in the parent at the time the parallel operation began.
 * The XIDs are stored sorted in numerical order (not logical order) to make
 * lookups as fast as possible.
 */

Japanese translation

 * トップレベルトランザクションで発生したイベントを記録するためのその他のフラグビット。

/*

		 * xid なしでコミットレコードを発行することはできず、また xid の割り当てを強制することも避けたい（例えば vacuum などで問題になるため）。
		 * そのため、無効化のための専用レコードを発行する。コミットレコードが発行される場合にはそれを使いたくないため、コミットと同期して発生するようにしている（WAL レコードをこれ以上発行したくないという理由もある）。
		 *
		 * XXX この機能の既知の用途はすべて欠陥である。XID は無効化を促した変更の可視性を制御するものではないため、このトランザクションがアボートした場合でも、他のセッションには無効化が必要となる。
		 *
		 * ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS は非トランザクション的な index_build() を実行し、これが relcache の無効化をキューに入れる。これには、(空の) テーブルを読み取った xid なしのトランザクションも含まれる。

Original comment

/*
		 * Transactions without an assigned xid can contain invalidation
		 * messages.  While inplace updates do this, this is not known to be
		 * necessary; see comment at inplace CacheInvalidateHeapTuple().
		 * Extensions might still rely on this capability, and standbys may
		 * need to process those invals.  We can't emit a commit record
		 * without an xid, and we don't want to force assigning an xid,
		 * because that'd be problematic for e.g. vacuum.  Hence we emit a
		 * bespoke record for the invalidations. We don't want to use that in
		 * case a commit record is emitted, so they happen synchronously with
		 * commits (besides not wanting to emit more WAL records).
		 *
		 * XXX Every known use of this capability is a defect.  Since an XID
		 * isn't controlling visibility of the change that prompted invals,
		 * other sessions need the inval even if this transactions aborts.
		 *
		 * ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS does a nontransactional index_build(), which
		 * queues a relcache inval, including in transactions without an xid
		 * that had read the (empty) table.  Standbys don't need any ON COMMIT
		 * DELETE ROWS invals, but we've not done the work to withhold them.
		 */

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:1418-1434

/*
		 * 自らを「コミットクリティカルセクション」内にあるものとしてマークする。
		 * これにより、並行するチェックポイントは、pg_xact を更新し終えるまで待機させられる。
		 * これを行わないと、チェックポイントが XLOG レコードの後に REDO を設定しても、
		 * pg_xact の更新をディスクにフラッシュできず、その直後にシステムがクラッシュした場合に
		 * トランザクションコミットが失われる可能性がある。
		 *
		 * 注: RecordTransactionAbort でこのフラグを設定することも可能だが、あえて行っていない。
		 * トランザクションの中止が失われても重要ではないためである。いずれにせよ、
		 * 中止されたものとみなされるためである。
		 *
		 * 自身のバックエンドの delayChkptFlags フラグを変更する際、ProcArrayLock を
		 * 保持する必要はない。これを変更するのは自分自身だけだからである。
		 * これにより、チェックポイント側でどのトランザクションがチェックポイントを
		 * 遅延させているかの判定が多少曖昧になるが、問題はない。
		 */

Original comment

/*
		 * Mark ourselves as within our "commit critical section".  This
		 * forces any concurrent checkpoint to wait until we've updated
		 * pg_xact.  Without this, it is possible for the checkpoint to set
		 * REDO after the XLOG record but fail to flush the pg_xact update to
		 * disk, leading to loss of the transaction commit if the system
		 * crashes a little later.
		 *
		 * Note: we could, but don't bother to, set this flag in
		 * RecordTransactionAbort.  That's because loss of a transaction abort
		 * is noncritical; the presumption would be that it aborted, anyway.
		 *
		 * It's safe to change the delayChkptFlags flag of our own backend
		 * without holding the ProcArrayLock, since we're the only one
		 * modifying it.  This makes checkpoint's determination of which xacts
		 * are delaying the checkpoint a bit fuzzy, but it doesn't matter.
		 */

/*
	 * 非同期でコミットするかどうかを確認する。synchronous_commit=off の場合、あるいは現在のトランザクションが WAL に記録される操作を行っていないか、xid を割り当てていない場合は、XLOG のフラッシュを非同期に行うことができる。トランザクションは、一時テーブルやログ出力されないテーブルにのみ書き込んだ場合、xid を持っていても WAL を書き込まないことがある。また、HOT プルーニングを行った場合は、xid がなくても WAL を書き込むことがある。クラッシュが発生した場合、そのようなトランザクションの消失は問題にならない。一時テーブルはいずれにせよ失われ、ログ出力されないテーブルは切り詰められ、HOT プルーニングは後で再度行われるためである。（以上のことから、この場合に XLOG レコードを出力する必要はないと考えるかもしれないが、現在はそのようにはしていない。少なくとも Hot Standby モードでは、KnownAssignedXids メカニズムがすべての XID 割り当てを追跡する必要があるため、確実に問題が発生するだろう。wal_level < replica の場合のみスキップしても問題ないかもしれないが、現時点ではそうしていない。）
	 *
	 * ただし、一時テーブル以外のリレーションのクリーンアップを行っている場合や、同期コミットを強制するコマンドをコミットしている場合は、XLOG を直ちにフラッシュしなければならない。（削除対象の一時テーブル以外のテーブルがある場合、COMMIT レコードがディスクにフラッシュされる前にファイルを削除してしまう可能性があるため、非同期コミットを許可してはならない。ただし、削除対象のテーブルがすべて一時テーブルである場合は、クラッシュ時にいずれにせよ失われるため、非同期コミットを許可している。）
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * Check if we want to commit asynchronously.  We can allow the XLOG flush
	 * to happen asynchronously if synchronous_commit=off, or if the current
	 * transaction has not performed any WAL-logged operation or didn't assign
	 * an xid.  The transaction can end up not writing any WAL, even if it has
	 * an xid, if it only wrote to temporary and/or unlogged tables.  It can
	 * end up having written WAL without an xid if it did HOT pruning.  In
	 * case of a crash, the loss of such a transaction will be irrelevant;
	 * temp tables will be lost anyway, unlogged tables will be truncated and
	 * HOT pruning will be done again later. (Given the foregoing, you might
	 * think that it would be unnecessary to emit the XLOG record at all in
	 * this case, but we don't currently try to do that.  It would certainly
	 * cause problems at least in Hot Standby mode, where the
	 * KnownAssignedXids machinery requires tracking every XID assignment.  It
	 * might be OK to skip it only when wal_level < replica, but for now we
	 * don't.)
	 *
	 * However, if we're doing cleanup of any non-temp rels or committing any
	 * command that wanted to force sync commit, then we must flush XLOG
	 * immediately.  (We must not allow asynchronous commit if there are any
	 * non-temp tables to be deleted, because we might delete the files before
	 * the COMMIT record is flushed to disk.  We do allow asynchronous commit
	 * if all to-be-deleted tables are temporary though, since they are lost
	 * anyway if we crash.)
	 */

	 * streaming replication because if we don't flush WAL regularly we will

/*
	 * これらはすべてコミット後のクリーンアップである。ここでエラーが発生した場合、
	 * トランザクションを中断するには遅すぎることに注意すること。これらは重要度の低い

	 * 他のバックエンドから見えるリソース（例：ファイル、バッファピン）を解放し、
	 * 次にロックを解放し、最後にバックエンドローカルなリソースを解放する。
	 * 我々を待機している他のバックエンドが、我々のトランザクションが完全に
	 * クリーンアップされたと認識する時点でロックを解放したいのである。
	 *
	 * 個々のクエリに関連付けられるリソースは、ResourceOwnerメカニズムによって
	 * 処理される。ここでの他の呼び出しは、バックエンド全体の状態に関するものである。
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * This is all post-commit cleanup.  Note that if an error is raised here,
	 * it's too late to abort the transaction.  This should be just
	 * noncritical resource releasing.
	 *
	 * The ordering of operations is not entirely random.  The idea is:
	 * release resources visible to other backends (eg, files, buffer pins);
	 * then release locks; then release backend-local resources. We want to
	 * release locks at the point where any backend waiting for us will see
	 * our transaction as being fully cleaned up.
	 *
	 * Resources that can be associated with individual queries are handled by
	 * the ResourceOwner mechanism.  The other calls here are for backend-wide
	 * state.
	 */

	 * このトランザクション内で一時テーブルにアクセスした場合は、PREPARE TRANSACTION を許可しない。
	 * 準備されたトランザクションが他のバックエンドの一時テーブルのロックを保持し続けることは、
	 * 例えばそのバックエンドの終了を妨げる可能性があるため、好ましくない。
	 * また、準備されたトランザクションに一時テーブルの DROP が含まれている場合に、
	 * ソースとなるバックエンドのローカルバッファや ON COMMIT 状態をどのようにクリーンアップするかなど、
	 * 他にも問題がある。
	 *
	 * 関数、演算子、拡張などの他のオブジェクト型も同様の制限を共有する。これらは作成、ロック、
	 * または削除されるべきではない。なぜなら、現在のセッションや、同じ一時名前空間を使用しようとする
	 * 後続のセッションに悪影響を及ぼす可能性があるからである。
	 *
	 * ON COMMIT アクションを実行した後でも一時リレーションにアクセスする可能性があるため、
	 * このチェックはそれらの実行後に行わなければならない。
	 *
	 * XXX 原則として、トランザクション内で作成および削除が完結する一時テーブルなど、
	 * いくつかの有用な特殊ケースについては制限を緩和できる可能性がある。
	 * ただし、それにはより多くの管理が必要になると思われる。
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * Don't allow PREPARE TRANSACTION if we've accessed a temporary table in
	 * this transaction.  Having the prepared xact hold locks on another
	 * backend's temp table seems a bad idea --- for instance it would prevent
	 * the backend from exiting.  There are other problems too, such as how to
	 * clean up the source backend's local buffers and ON COMMIT state if the
	 * prepared xact includes a DROP of a temp table.
	 *
	 * Other objects types, like functions, operators or extensions, share the
	 * same restriction as they should not be created, locked or dropped as
	 * this can mess up with this session or even a follow-up session trying
	 * to use the same temporary namespace.
	 *
	 * We must check this after executing any ON COMMIT actions, because they
	 * might still access a temp relation.
	 *
	 * XXX In principle this could be relaxed to allow some useful special
	 * cases, such as a temp table created and dropped all within the
	 * transaction.  That seems to require much more bookkeeping though.
	 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:2618-2622

/*
	 * 同様に、pg_export_snapshot の後の PREPARE も許可しない。
	 * twophase.c にクリーンアップロジックを追加すればサポート可能だが、
	 * 現時点ではその手間をかける価値はないと思われる。
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * Likewise, don't allow PREPARE after pg_export_snapshot.  This could be

/*
	 * 2PC状態ファイル用のデータを収集する。一般的に、このステップ中に呼び出されるモジュールで実際の状態変更が発生すべきではないことに注意すること。コミット前に失敗する可能性があるためであり、その場合はトランザクションの中断によってクリーンアップできるようにする必要がある。（特に、AtPrepareルーチンは、処理できないケースを見つけた場合にエラーを返す可能性がある。）状態のクリーンアップは、以下のPostPrepareルーチンで行う必要がある。ただし、一部のモジュールは、中断時に状態を使用しないため、ここで状態をクリアしても問題ない。
	 *
	 * 注: 2PC状態ファイルのレコードは作成された順序でリプレイされるため、これらの呼び出し順序は、COMMIT PREPAREDまたはROLLBACK PREPAREDの間に実行したい順序と一致させる必要がある。特に、トランザクションのロックを解放する前に行うべきか、後に行うべきかに注意すること。
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * Collect data for the 2PC state file.  Note that in general, no actual
	 * state change should happen in the called modules during this step,
	 * since it's still possible to fail before commit, and in that case we
	 * want transaction abort to be able to clean up.  (In particular, the
	 * AtPrepare routines may error out if they find cases they cannot
	 * handle.)  State cleanup should happen in the PostPrepare routines
	 * below.  However, some modules can go ahead and clear state here because
	 * they wouldn't do anything with it during abort anyway.
	 *
	 * Note: because the 2PC state file records will be replayed in the same
	 * order they are made, the order of these calls has to match the order in
	 * which we want things to happen during COMMIT PREPARED or ROLLBACK
	 * PREPARED; in particular, pay attention to whether things should happen
	 * before or after releasing the transaction's locks.
	 */

/*
 * Simple system for saving and restoring transaction characteristics

 * GUC system resets the characteristics at transaction end, so for example
 * just skipping the reset in StartTransaction() won't work.)
 */

 *
 *	このルーチンは、トランザクションブロック内で実行してはならないステートメントによって呼び出される。
 *	これは通常、ロールバック不可能な副作用があるか、内部でコミットを行うためである。

 *	このルーチンが正常に完了した場合、呼び出し元のステートメントは、エラーなしで完了すれば
 *	その結果が即座にコミットされることが保証される。

 *	すでにトランザクションブロックが開始されている場合はエラーを発行する。また、ユーザー定義関数内で

 *	失敗を引き起こす可能性があるため）。サブトランザクションも禁止されている。

 *	また、MyXactFlags に XACT_FLAGS_NEEDIMMEDIATECOMMIT を設定し、postgres.c がステートメント完了後に
 *	確実にコミットするようにしなければならない。
 *
 *	isTopLevel: 関数内にいるかどうかを判断するために ProcessUtility から渡される。

 */

Original comment

/*
 *	PreventInTransactionBlock
 *
 *	This routine is to be called by statements that must not run inside
 *	a transaction block, typically because they have non-rollback-able
 *	side effects or do internal commits.
 *
 *	If this routine completes successfully, then the calling statement is
 *	guaranteed that if it completes without error, its results will be
 *	committed immediately.
 *
 *	If we have already started a transaction block, issue an error; also issue
 *	an error if we appear to be running inside a user-defined function (which
 *	could issue more commands and possibly cause a failure after the statement
 *	completes).  Subtransactions are verboten too.
 *
 *	We must also set XACT_FLAGS_NEEDIMMEDIATECOMMIT in MyXactFlags, to ensure
 *	that postgres.c follows through by committing after the statement is done.
 *
 *	isTopLevel: passed down from ProcessUtility to determine whether we are
 *	inside a function.  (We will always fail if this is false, but it's
 *	convenient to centralize the check here instead of making callers do it.)
 *	stmtType: statement type name, for error messages.
 */

Japanese translation

/*
 *	WarnNoTransactionBlock
 *	RequireTransactionBlock
 *
 *	これら2つの関数は、コマンドがトランザクションブロックの外側で実行された場合に警告またはエラーを出すためのものです。
 *	これは、トランザクション終了後も持続する効果を持たないコマンド（したがって、トランザクションブロックの外側で呼び出すことはおそらく誤りである）に対して有用です。
 *	DECLARE CURSORがその例です。
 *	トップレベルのトランザクション制御コマンド（BEGIN/COMMIT/ABORT）や効果のないSETは警告を発行しますが、その他の効果のないコマンドはすべてエラーを生成します。
 *
 *	ユーザー定義関数内で実行されているように見える場合は、何も発行しません。なぜなら、その関数が現在のステートメントの結果を利用するさらなるコマンドを発行する可能性があるためです。サブトランザクションも同様です。
 *	したがって、これらはPreventInTransactionBlockの逆の動作となります。
 *
 *	isTopLevel: 関数内かどうかを判断するためにProcessUtilityから渡されます。
 *	stmtType: 警告またはエラーメッセージ用のステートメントタイプ名。
 */

Original comment

/*
 *	WarnNoTransactionBlock
 *	RequireTransactionBlock
 *
 *	These two functions allow for warnings or errors if a command is executed
 *	outside of a transaction block.  This is useful for commands that have no
 *	effects that persist past transaction end (and so calling them outside a
 *	transaction block is presumably an error).  DECLARE CURSOR is an example.
 *	While top-level transaction control commands (BEGIN/COMMIT/ABORT) and SET
 *	that have no effect issue warnings, all other no-effect commands generate
 *	errors.
 *
 *	If we appear to be running inside a user-defined function, we do not
 *	issue anything, since the function could issue more commands that make
 *	use of the current statement's results.  Likewise subtransactions.
 *	Thus these are inverses for PreventInTransactionBlock.
 *
 *	isTopLevel: passed down from ProcessUtility to determine whether we are
 *	inside a function.
 *	stmtType: statement type name, for warning or error messages.
 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:3721-3723

/*
 * これらは上記2つの実装です。
 */

Original comment

/*
 * This is the implementation of the above two.
 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:3752-3767

/*
 *	IsInTransactionBlock
 *
 *	このルーチンは、単一コマンドとして実行される場合とトランザクションブロック内で実行される場合で動作を変える必要があるステートメントのためのものです。現在、ANALYZE が唯一の例です。
 *
 *	このルーチンが "false" を返す場合、呼び出し元のステートメントは内部的なトランザクションのコミットと開始のサイクルを実行することが許可されます。進行中のトランザクションを壊すリスクはありません。（なお、これは PreventInTransactionBlock が提供する保証と同一ではありません。ステートメント実行後のコミットを強制するわけではないためです。）
 *
 *	isTopLevel: 関数内かどうかを判断するために ProcessUtility から渡されます。
 */

Original comment

/*
 *	IsInTransactionBlock
 *
 *	This routine is for statements that need to behave differently inside
 *	a transaction block than when running as single commands.  ANALYZE is
 *	currently the only example.
 *
 *	If this routine returns "false", then the calling statement is allowed
 *	to perform internal transaction-commit-and-start cycles; there is not a
 *	risk of messing up any transaction already in progress.  (Note that this
 *	is not the identical guarantee provided by PreventInTransactionBlock,
 *	since we will not force a post-statement commit.)
 *
 *	isTopLevel: passed down from ProcessUtility to determine whether we are
 *	inside a function.
 */

Japanese translation

 * トランザクション開始時および終了時の操作に対するコールバック関数を登録または登録解除する。
 *
 * これらの関数は、動的にロードされるモジュールによる使用を意図している。
 * 組み込みモジュールについては、通常、適切な呼び出しを直接ハードコードする（主に、必要に応じて順序を制御する方が容易であるため）。
 *
 * トランザクション終了時、コールバックはコミット後またはアボート後に発生するため、コールバック関数は重要度の低いクリーンアップのみを実行できる。
 */

Original comment

/*
 * Register or deregister callback functions for start- and end-of-xact
 * operations.
 *
 * These functions are intended for use by dynamically loaded modules.
 * For built-in modules we generally just hardwire the appropriate calls
 * (mainly because it's easier to control the order that way, where needed).
 *
 * At transaction end, the callback occurs post-commit or post-abort, so the
 * callback functions can only do noncritical cleanup.
 */

/*
			 * 暗黙のトランザクションブロック内でのセーブポイントコマンドは許可しない。
			 * このモジュールに関する限り、許可すること自体に大きな困難はないが、
			 * エラー発生時にクエリ文字列全体を破棄するという exec_simple_query の動作と、
			 * セーブポイントは矛盾しているように思われる。また、暗黙のトランザクションブロック
			 * （通常のトランザクションブロックとは対照的に）の目的は、エラー後に自動的に
			 * クローズすることであるため、そこにセーブポイントがどのように適合するのかは不明である。
			 *
			 * この件に関するエラーメッセージは、アクティブなトランザクションブロックが
			 * 全く存在しないかのように表現されているが、これは歴史的な経緯によるものであり、
			 * おそらく改善の余地がある。
			 */

Original comment

/*
			 * We disallow savepoint commands in implicit transaction blocks.
			 * There would be no great difficulty in allowing them so far as
			 * this module is concerned, but a savepoint seems inconsistent
			 * with exec_simple_query's behavior of abandoning the whole query
			 * string upon error.  Also, the point of an implicit transaction
			 * block (as opposed to a regular one) is to automatically close
			 * after an error, so it's hard to see how a savepoint would fit
			 * into that.
			 *
			 * The error messages for this are phrased as if there were no
			 * active transaction block at all, which is historical but
			 * perhaps could be improved.
			 */

/*
 * StartSubTransaction
 *
 * If you're wondering why this is separate from PushTransaction: it's because
 * we can't conveniently do this stuff right inside DefineSavepoint.  The
 * SAVEPOINT utility command will be executed inside a Portal, and if we
 * muck with CurrentMemoryContext or CurrentResourceOwner then exit from
 * the Portal will undo those settings.  So we make DefineSavepoint just
 * push a dummy transaction block, and when control returns to the main
 * idle loop, CommitTransactionCommand will be called, and we'll come here
 * to finish starting the subtransaction.
 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:6221-6235

/*
		 * まず、このWALレコードをカバーするように最小リカバリポイントを更新する。リレーションが削除されると、元に戻すことはできない。バッファマネージャは、リレーションファイルへの通常の更新に対してWALファースト・ルールを強制するため、データファイルの対応する変更がディスクにフラッシュされる前に最小リカバリポイントが常に更新される。しかし、ここではバッファマネージャをバイパスしているため、同様の処理を自分たちで行う必要がある。
		 *
		 * ファイルを削除する前にこれを行うということは、何らかの理由で削除が失敗した場合、削除が成功するように根本的な状況を修正しない限り、再起動後であってもシステムを起動できないことを意味する。あるいは、削除後に最小リカバリポイントを更新することも可能だが、それではWALファースト・ルールが破られる小さな隙間が生じてしまう。
		 */

Original comment

/*
		 * First update minimum recovery point to cover this WAL record. Once
		 * a relation is deleted, there's no going back. The buffer manager
		 * enforces the WAL-first rule for normal updates to relation files,
		 * so that the minimum recovery point is always updated before the
		 * corresponding change in the data file is flushed to disk, but we
		 * have to do the same here since we're bypassing the buffer manager.
		 *
		 * Doing this before deleting the files means that if a deletion fails
		 * for some reason, you cannot start up the system even after restart,
		 * until you fix the underlying situation so that the deletion will
		 * succeed. Alternatively, we could update the minimum recovery point
		 * after deletion, but that would leave a small window where the
		 * WAL-first rule would be violated.
		 */

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:6250-6261

/*
	 * 通常の運用で ForceSyncCommit() を発行するのと同じ理由で、XLogFlush() を発行する。
	 * 例えば、CREATE DATABASE では、テンプレートデータベースからすべてのファイルをコピーし、
	 * その後にトランザクションをコミットする。すべてのファイルがコピーされた後、
	 * コミットされる前にクラッシュした場合、pg_database にエントリがないまま
	 * データディレクトリにファイルが存在することになる。この期間を最小限に抑えるため、
	 * ForceSyncCommit() を使用してコミットレコードを可能な限り迅速にディスクへ書き込む。
	 * リカバリ中も同様の期間が存在し、XLogFlush() を強制する（リカバリ中に
	 * minRecoveryPoint を更新する）ことは、ForceSyncCommit() を要求したユーザーに対して、
	 * その問題が発生する期間を短縮するのに役立つ。
	 */

Original comment

/*
	 * We issue an XLogFlush() for the same reason we emit ForceSyncCommit()
	 * in normal operation. For example, in CREATE DATABASE, we copy all files
	 * from the template database, and then commit the transaction. If we
	 * crash after all the files have been copied but before the commit, you
	 * have files in the data directory without an entry in pg_database. To
	 * minimize the window for that, we use ForceSyncCommit() to rush the
	 * commit record to disk as quick as possible. We have the same window
	 * during recovery, and forcing an XLogFlush() (which updates
	 * minRecoveryPoint during recovery) helps to reduce that problem window,
	 * for any user that requested ForceSyncCommit().
	 */

Japanese translation

src/backend/access/transam/xact.c:6274-6282

/*
 * xact_redo_commit() と同様に、実行順序には注意すること。
 * 両関数は似ているが、重要な箇所で異なっている。
 *
 * また、アボートはトップレベルのアボートだけでなく、サブトランザクションとその子トランザクションに対しても発生し得ることに注意。
 * つまり、topxid != xid の場合を考慮する必要がある。一方、コミットの場合はサブトランザクションのコミットはWALログに記録されないため、常に topxid == xid となる。
 */

Original comment

/*
 * Be careful with the order of execution, as with xact_redo_commit().
 * The two functions are similar but differ in key places.
 *
 * Note also that an abort can be for a subtransaction and its children,
 * not just for a top level abort. That means we have to consider
 * topxid != xid, whereas in commit we would find topxid == xid always
 * because subtransaction commit is never WAL logged.
 */
